- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- If sentiment shifts sharply upward (e.g., +0.67+ in 1–2 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and news volume drops to 0, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% of recent mean.
- Model frequently lags in high-news-volume periods; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast for each day of news volume >0.
- In mean-reversion zones (sentiment neutral, price oscillating), model tends to hold too low; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with recent high.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >2.0% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “spike correction” — add 0.5–1.0% to next forecast to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often underestimates; add 0.3–0.8% to forecast to compensate for sentiment decay.
